hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: A sharp array strictly alternates between peaks and valleys: nums[0] < nums[1] > nums[2] < nums[3]...

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: The minimum deletions to obtain a sharp sequence equals the original length minus the length of the longest alternating subsequence.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Track alternating direction changes across adjacent elements greedily.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def minDeletionsToMakeSharp(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(nums)
    if n <= 1:
        return 0

    # Longest alternating subsequence (wiggle) starting with an increase
    # up: max length ending with an increase
    # down: max length ending with a decrease
    up = 1
    down = 1

    for i in range(1, n):
        if nums[i] > nums[i - 1]:
            up = down + 1
        elif nums[i] < nums[i - 1]:
            down = up + 1

    longest_sharp = max(up, down)
    return n - longest_sharp
```

complexity.notes: Single pass greedy count of turning points gives maximum sharp subsequence length.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all 2^n deletion subsets is exponential.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies equivalence to length minus longest wiggle subsequence.
